## Companies Building Food from Fermentation

A growing number of companies — from startups to global food giants — are using fermentation technologies (traditional, biomass, and precision fermentation) to produce food ingredients and finished products. Here is an overview of the key players:

---

### Precision Fermentation Pioneers (Animal-Free Proteins & Ingredients)

- **Perfect Day, Inc.** — Founded in 2014, headquartered in Berkeley, California. Produces animal-free whey protein via precision fermentation for use in ice cream, milk, and cream cheese. The company has also formalized an enterprise services business called "nth" to offer end-to-end fermentation expertise and manufacturing services to partners. Investors include Presight Capital, ICONIQ Capital, and Synthesis Capital.

- **Remilk** — Focuses on high-volume manufacturing of animal-free dairy proteins using precision fermentation.

- **New Culture** — Produces animal-free casein specifically for making authentic mozzarella cheese.

- **The Every Co.** — Makes animal-free egg white proteins through fermentation; has raised nearly $300 million over the past decade.

- **Onego Bio** — Produces egg white protein without chickens using precision fermentation.

- **Geltor** — Maker of fermentation-derived collagens (including HumaColl21 and Collume); raised $91.3 million to develop animal-free gelatin products.

- **Fooditive BV** (Rotterdam, Netherlands) — Turns microbes into animal-free casein for dairy and a zero-calorie sweetener, licensed to global food and beverage manufacturers. Won $500,000 in the 2026 Grow-NY competition.

---

### Biomass & Gas Fermentation (Novel Proteins)

- **Solar Foods Oyj** — Finnish biotech company founded in 2017, headquartered in Vantaa, Finland. Develops **Solein**, a microbial protein produced by feeding microbes CO₂, hydrogen, and oxygen — resulting in a neutral-flavoured powder with ~78% protein. Backed by Voima Ventures, Nordic FoodTech VC, Agronomics, and Business Finland.

- **Meati Foods** — Grows whole-cut meat alternatives from mycelium (mushroom root); raised funding to expand production of its steak alternative.

- **NOIET** — Develops multifunctional clean-label ingredients rich in protein and fiber through proprietary multi-microbial fermentation of plant-based by-products.

- **Onima** — Transforms spent brewer's yeast into a premium protein and nutrition ingredient via a patented bioprocess.

---

### Fermentation-Derived Fats, Sugars & Specialty Ingredients

- **C16 Biosciences** — Has introduced a precision-fermented cocoa butter equivalent as its first food ingredient.

- **Zero Acre Farms** — Creates alternative oils produced by microorganisms and fermentation; raised $37 million.

- **Yali Bio** — Uses microbes to make fats efficiently; building a microbial strain library for fermentation-based fat production.

- **Amyris** — Synbio pioneer with vertically integrated biomanufacturing; recently acquired **Oobli**, which uses precision fermentation to produce sweet proteins as a sugar alternative.

---

### Established Food & Ingredient Companies Active in Fermentation

- **Lesaffre** — Develops fermentation solutions for baking, taste, and nutrition.

- **Kerry Group** — Provides fermentation solutions, probiotics, starter cultures, enzymes, and microbial tools for food and industrial bioprocessing.

- **Danone** — One of the world's most influential companies in fermented dairy and probiotic foods.

- **Ajinomoto** — Uses precision fermentation to produce amino acids, flavors, and food ingredients at scale.

- **dsm-firmenich** — Major global ingredient and nutrition company with deep fermentation capabilities.

- **Angel Yeast** — Leading yeast and biotechnology company supporting food and beverage fermentation.

- **Novozymes / DuPont** — Developing fermentation-derived product lines for the alternative protein industry.

- **Kraft Heinz** — Has launched fermentation R&D under its "Future of Food" initiatives, led by a dedicated Next Generation Ingredients team.

- **Nestlé** — Has partnered with Perfect Day to research animal-free protein using precision fermentation.

---

### Infrastructure & Scale-Up Enablers

- **Planetary** (Geneva, Switzerland) — Building industrial-scale production facilities so food-tech companies can scale fermentation-based alternative proteins.

- **Biotechnology Fermentation Factory (BFF)** — Open-access facility at the NIZO Food Innovation Campus in the Netherlands, offering food-grade precision and biomass fermentation upscaling with support from GEA.

- **Ginkgo Bioworks / Motif FoodWorks** — Building an ingredient platform business for fermentation-derived food ingredients.

---

The fermentation-for-food sector spans three main approaches: **traditional fermentation** (yogurt, cheese, bread), **biomass fermentation** (growing microorganisms as the food itself, e.g., mycoprotein), and **precision fermentation** (programming microbes to produce specific proteins, fats, or other molecules). Investment and corporate partnerships continue to grow, with the sector positioned as a key pillar of sustainable food production.
